newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's king arrives in PLO-ruled Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king arrives in PLO-ruled Gaza.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan arrived on his first visit to the PLO-ruled Gaza Strip on Sunday, showing solidarity with the Palestinians while peace talks with Israel falter, witnesses said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat greeted the king.
"This is a great honour and encouragement from him to push the peace process forward and to strengthen the Palestinian-Jordanian relationship," Arafat told Israel Radio earlier on Sunday.

The Jordanian monarch visited the self-ruled enclave of Jericho in the West Bank -- which the king lost to Israel in a 1967 war -- last October. He arrived with Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.

Arafat's cabinet said in a statement late on Saturday that U.S.-brokered peace talks with Israel to launch self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron were near a dead-end. U.S. envoy Dennis Ross was due to leave the region on Sunday after failing to clinch a deal between the sides in a three week shuttle.

The king landed at Arafat's office in Gaza City after Israel refused a Palestinian request to receive the monarch's helicopter at an airport in the south of the strip. Israel demands security control of the airport.
